security_audit.summary: Most analyzer hits are false positives caused by the Python alias ln, Markdown backticks, placeholders, and documentation links. Confirmed risks include default MinIO credentials, plaintext HTTP, permissive shared-cache access, shared temporary storage, and unguarded recursive deletion. Database passwords in command arguments and unprotected database backups are additional context-level risks.

remediation.issue: Examples use the public MinIO default credential pair.
remediation.suggestion: Replace defaults with generated placeholders and require unique secrets before starting MinIO.

remediation.issue: Shared cache permissions allow traversal by every local user.
remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated group and mode 750 or 770, then document restrictive file creation permissions.

remediation.issue: Several S3-compatible storage examples use plaintext HTTP.
remediation.suggestion: Use HTTPS endpoints with certificate verification, except for clearly labeled isolated local development.

remediation.issue: Cache cleanup recursively deletes an unchecked configured path.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer LaminDB cache APIs, resolve the path, verify it is the cache directory, and request confirmation before recursive deletion.

remediation.issue: Migration examples use a predictable shared temporary directory.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with restrictive permissions, reject links, validate imported files, and remove the directory after migration.

remediation.issue: PostgreSQL passwords are shown inside command-line URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Use a protected password file, secret manager, or interactive prompt so credentials do not enter shell history.

remediation.issue: The database backup example creates an unprotected local dump.
remediation.suggestion: Write backups into a restricted directory with umask 077, encryption, retention controls, and tested secure restoration procedures.

content.value_statement: Biological data workflows often lose metadata, lineage, and consistent annotations. This skill provides LaminDB guidance for organizing, validating, querying, tracing, integrating, and deploying research data.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to create, version, query, stream, and organize LaminDB artifacts and collections.
Guides schema validation for DataFrame, AnnData, MuData, SpatialData, and TileDB-SOMA datasets.
Shows ontology workflows for genes, cell types, tissues, diseases, and other Bionty registries.
Provides lineage patterns for notebooks, scripts, Nextflow, Snakemake, and Redun workflows.
Documents integrations with W&B, MLflow, Hugging Face, scVI-tools, Vitessce, DuckDB, and Git.
Covers local, SQLite, PostgreSQL, S3, GCS, MinIO, and Cloudflare R2 setup options.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples but does not execute LaminDB operations by itself.
Requires LaminDB and access to each configured database, storage system, and third-party service.
Examples may require adaptation for your LaminDB version, schema, permissions, and infrastructure.
Does not replace security, privacy, or regulatory review for biological or clinical data.

use_cases.title: Curate single-cell datasets
use_cases.description: Build validation and ontology workflows for AnnData metadata before analysis or sharing.

use_cases.title: Build a biological data lakehouse
use_cases.description: Organize versioned artifacts, searchable features, collections, and lineage across local or cloud storage.

use_cases.title: Track computational pipelines
use_cases.description: Connect workflow runs, inputs, outputs, parameters, models, and experiment platforms for reproducible research.

prompt_templates.title: Create a local instance
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me install LaminDB, initialize local storage at [path], register [dataset type], and explain each verification step.

prompt_templates.title: Curate an annotated dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LaminDB curation workflow for [dataset type] with required columns [columns] and ontology-backed fields [fields].

prompt_templates.title: Track a research pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a tracked [workflow manager] pipeline that loads [inputs], records parameters, saves [outputs], and preserves code and data lineage.

prompt_templates.title: Design production infrastructure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production LaminDB deployment using [storage], [database], [identity provider], and [regions], including migration, access control, backups, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Plan a local LaminDB setup for ten AnnData files with cell type validation.
output_examples.output: A staged setup plan covering environment creation, local instance initialization, AnnData registration, Bionty validation, artifact annotation, and lineage verification.

output_examples.input: Show how a team can query treated PBMC datasets without loading every file.
output_examples.output: A metadata-first query strategy using hierarchical keys, typed tissue and condition features, filtered artifact records, and selective loading.

output_examples.input: Design a secure migration from local SQLite storage to S3 and PostgreSQL.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist covering backups, private staging, managed credentials, encrypted connections, access policies, validation, rollback, and post-migration monitoring.

best_practices: Define schemas and ontology-backed features before registering large datasets.
Track every workflow run with explicit inputs, parameters, outputs, and descriptive artifact metadata.
Query metadata before loading files, and use private encrypted storage for sensitive research data.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode credentials, default passwords, or database secrets in commands and notebooks.
Do not delete caches, artifacts, or instances without validating scope and preserving required backups.
Do not treat example deployment settings as production-ready without reviewing permissions, encryption, privacy, and compliance.

faq.question: What data types does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers files, DataFrames, AnnData, MuData, SpatialData, TileDB-SOMA, Parquet, Zarr, and related biological artifacts.

faq.question: Can it help with biological ontologies?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Bionty imports, validation, synonym standardization, hierarchy navigation, and ontology-backed annotations.

faq.question: Does it support cloud storage?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents S3, GCS, MinIO, Cloudflare R2, local storage, SQLite, and PostgreSQL configurations.

faq.question: Can it execute migrations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides migration guidance and examples, while users must review and run operations in their environment.

faq.question: Does it replace a privacy review?
faq.answer: No. Biological and clinical data still require appropriate governance, consent, access control, and regulatory review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
